2. Facts leading to this in short are that M/S. Ahmedia Garments instituted a suit in the 3rd subordinate Judge Dhaka being money suit No. 116 of 1985 for a decree for realization of Tk. 24,56,828/- against the defendant oppose parties No. 1 and 2 namely M/S Yama Moto & Co. Ltd., a company situated with its head office at Japan and pioneer industrial, authorized agent of M/S.YAMA MOTO for damages and compensation on the ground that the plaintiff while carrying on the business of manufacturing various types of ready made garments for export and also for local sale, in order to modernism the said garment industry intended to import machineries from the defendant No.1 and accordingly opened an irrevocable letter of credit in Janata Bank being l/C. No. NDS/NO/84/JBD/LEF/18/84 dated 10.10.84 for importing machineries and accessories for garment industry under deferred payment against indent No. KB/RG/J/097/84 dated 16.8.1984 issued by M/S. UAMA MOTO & CO's agent in Dhaka namely pioneer International. The plaintiff opened another letter of credit being D/C No. HDS/NG/JBD/DEF/19/84 dated 3.12.1984 for importing more garment machineries under the same deferred payment system against indent No. KB/RG/J/097/84 dated 16.8.84 issued by the said M/S Pioneer International M/S. UAMA MOTO & CO LTD., agreed to supply the garment machineries and other accessories 10 the plaintiff according to the Specifications as mentioned in the letter of credit and the indent and also agreed to fulfill the other terms and conditions as laid down in the said indent. 

 13. The Court upon a finding that the Janata Bank had failed to submit any paper to show that the defendant No. 1 the seller company had actually received the amount from the Bank of Tokyo and the photo copy of the Telex from the Bank of Tokyo Ltd. to Janata Bank stating that the amount in question had already been paid to defendant No.1 by the Bank of Tokyo are no papers to substantiate their claim and having found that the defendant opposite party did not submit any paper to show that they can pay the amount before maturity the court hold that the schedule amount is still lying with the Janata Bank and has not been paid to defendant No. 1 by the Bank of Tokyo Ltd. and having found that the said foreign company had no property in this country and their agent defendant No. 2 having no existence come to a finding that if the schedule amount is paid to the defendant No. 1 by the Janata Bank then the decree that might be passed cannot be executed and thereby the purpose of the suit shall be frustrated and thus the petition for attachment was allowed. 

 22. In the instant case it is a question of attachment before judgment as provided under Order 38 rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure. It provided that where, at any stage of a suit, the court is satisfied, by an affidavit or otherwise, that the defendant, with intent to obstruct or delay the execution of any decree that may be passed against him. 

 (b) is about to remove the whole or any part of his property from the local limits of the jurisdiction of the court, the court may direct the defendant, within a time to be fixed by it, either to furnish security in such sum as may be specified in the order, to produce and place at the disposal of the court, when required, the said property or the value of the same or such portion thereof as may be sufficient to satisfy the decree, or to appear and show cause why he should not furnish security. The Court in passing the show cause may order conditional attachment of the property. If no cause is shown and no security furnished the Court may order that the property or such portion may be attend. 

 23. It thus appears that it is the properly of the defendant in question in a money suit who may have to pay would. be attached for satisfaction of the decree that may be passed against him on condition that the court is satisfied that such property or whole of the properly is attempted to be disposed of or removed out of the jurisdiction of the Court to frustrate the decree and he has no other properly left to satisfy the decree. 

 58. In that Indian case under report Mr. M.C. Staved the learned Advocate appearing for the Indian firm had not controverted the said principle but very seriously urged, (as it is also argued and the only point argued in this case) for the respondent plaintiff that the Russian Firm has no assets in this country and therefore any decree that may be obtained against that Russian Firm cannot be executed. Hence they must be restrained from further dealing with the L.C. which promised to pay and the Bank for not honoring it.
